subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a former bookseller who assaulted the keeper of the tomes and was merely fired, not executed — a fact that has left him emotionally unmoored and prone to inappropriate mirth.
source_quote: He wasn't celebrating a murder. He was a man who had braced for annihilation and learned he was merely going to be fired, and the relief had gone straight to his head.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a methodical interrogator who uses patterned questioning to expose contradictions, and who recognizes the forensic significance of bodily habits — especially finger-licking and page-turning.
source_quote: We took it. We'd keep Daral close until midnight — a cleric who could draw poison out, and a sword that could do the same, both within arm's reach.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was the keeper of the tomes, a philistine who sought to sell priceless poetry to fund a worthless tome about demonic planes — and was poisoned via a book he licked while turning its pages.
source_quote: Janussi had been poisoned, the poison carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages.

subject: The Keepers of the Tome
fact: The Keepers of the Tome enforce a brutal, ritualistic justice: assaulting their keeper results in the complete annihilation of the offender’s bloodline — cousins, aunts, infants — to make the lesson legible.
source_quote: In the city, when you go for the big boss and miss, you die — and so does your bloodline, every cousin and aunt and infant, because the whole point of slaughtering them is to make the lesson legible.

subject: Poisoning of Janussi
fact: Janussi was poisoned through a book he licked while turning its pages — a method that implicates only someone who handled the book with direct oral contact.
source_quote: The dead poisoner is the innocent one. A man does not lace the pages he's been licking all night.

subject: The Book (formerly Daral's favorite)
fact: A treasured volume given by Daral to Janussi as a symbolic gesture — later found saturated with poison, licked and turned by Janussi, and now the key forensic artifact in his murder.
source_quote: He produced the book to prove it. And then, telling us how shaken the assault had left him, he wet his finger and began flicking through the pages, reading himself a funny passage until he was laughing again.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is a lizard-like creature, possibly a sentient entity that consumes books and their knowledge, with a predatory nature and a history of eating its young — suspected by Daral as a potential killer.
source_quote: There's no telling what's going on in her lizard brain. Cold-blooded, he went on, they eat their young, murdering crowbait like Janussi.

subject: Teles
fact: Teles is an elderly, deluded figure who covets the position of keeper of the tomes and is among the suspects in Janussi’s murder, per Daral’s paranoid accounting.
source_quote: The suspects spilled out between page-turns — Teles, the deluded old git;

subject: A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A'lai Aivenmore is a predatory, opportunistic individual who seeks the keeper’s position and is named by Daral as a suspect — described as a 'preying cock' in his paranoid taxonomy.
source_quote: A'lai Aivenmore, the preying cock;

subject: Fheminor Scrivenbark
fact: Fheminor Scrivenbark is a small-statured but formidable individual, dismissed by Daral as 'don't be fooled by her stature, she has a steely nature' — one of the suspects in Janussi’s murder.
source_quote: Fheminor Scrivenbark, don't be fooled by her stature, she has a steely nature.

subject: The True Nature of Daral's Laughter
fact: Daral’s laughter is not mere absurdity — it is the psychological residue of surviving a punishment system that should have killed him, and his mirth is the symptom of cognitive dissonance between expectation and reality.
source_quote: He deflected to the others — they wanted the top job, every one of them, Bookwyrm and Teles and A'lai and Fheminor, round and round.

subject: The Silent Lesson of Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s answer — 'The body that mimics nothing is already shaped by what it watches' — reveals a profound, untaught truth about absorption and identity that Zalthir failed to learn in class, despite having been present.
source_quote: Glabbagool held it like it was the easiest thing he had ever been asked to do.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a former shadow monk who missed the lesson on silent communication — now bonded with Glabbagool, an ooze entity who embodies the wisdom Zalthir never learned.
source_quote: The former shadow monk had been watching the whole exchange. He looked at me and said that if I had paid more attention to the classes on silent communication, I would know exactly what Glabbagool's answer meant.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient ooze entity capable of telepathic communication, acidic dissolution, and perfect stillness — now bonded to Zalthir as a symbiotic companion who embodies the silent wisdom he never learned.
source_quote: Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now, he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance.

subject: The Whispering Dome
fact: The Whispering Dome is a sacred space where supplicants undergo silent revelation — a place of profound quiet where truth is learned not through speech but through presence and stillness.
source_quote: The Dome is where supplicants go to learn something about themselves.

subject: Bonding of Glabbagool and Zalthir
fact: Glabbagool chose Zalthir as his host, not through force or ritual, but by slipping onto his arm and declaring their union — a moment that revealed Zalthir’s failure to understand silent communication.
source_quote: And he flowed up onto my arm. Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now, he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance.

subject: The Bag of Holding (with Drow)
fact: A container holding captured drow, which Glabbagool insists must be monitored — a detail that reveals his priorities: even in transformation, he remains a caretaker of responsibility.
source_quote: Before he settled in, he reminded me the drow in the bag of holding still needed watching.

subject: The Paradox of the Book
fact: Daral gave Janussi the book to teach its worth — then raged when Janussi read it — revealing a contradiction: he wanted the book to be understood, but not enjoyed — a theological dissonance that mirrors his own moral confusion.
source_quote: He'd given it away to make a point — that his books should never be sold — by having Janussi read it and understand their worth. And then he'd been enraged to find Janussi reading it.

subject: The Finger on the Page
fact: The act of wetting a finger and turning pages is not innocent — it is the vector of poison, the signature of the killer, and the unconscious habit of the innocent — making Daral both suspect and victim.
source_quote: I watched the finger go to the mouth and back to the paper. I was fairly sure I knew what I was watching.

subject: The Trial of Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s answer to 'What is the art of movement?' — 'The body that mimics nothing is already shaped by what it watches' — was accepted as wisdom, proving that true understanding arises not from instruction but from silent observation.
source_quote: The monk smiled. Nodded. Accepted it as wisdom, because it was.

subject: The Former Shadow Monk
fact: The former shadow monk is a silent observer who recognizes Zalthir’s failure to learn the lesson of silence — and implies that Zalthir’s bond with Glabbagool is the universe correcting his neglect.
source_quote: He looked at me and said that if I had paid more attention to the classes on silent communication, I would know exactly what Glabbagool's answer meant.

subject: Blingdenstone
fact: Blingdenstone is a subterranean refuge where Glabbagool survived an ooze crisis — a place of trauma and endurance that shaped his instinct for preservation even during transformation.
source_quote: He had survived Blingdenstone and the ooze crisis and however long in the dark, and his instinct, at the moment of his own transformation, was housekeeping.

subject: The Silence That Wasn't Learned
fact: Zalthir attended the class on silent communication but remembers nothing — while Glabbagool, an ooze, mastered it in a minute by doing nothing — revealing that wisdom is not taught, but absorbed.
source_quote: The student on my arm had mastered the one lesson I most thoroughly missed, and he had done it in under a minute, by going still.

subject: Who Really Killed Janussi?
fact: The true killer may be Daral — who licked the book’s pages and poisoned himself — or someone else who used his habit as a cover — making the act of reading a crime and the innocent the only one who could have done it.
source_quote: The dead poisoner is the innocent one.
